# Claude / Codex handoff: Commons experience

1 November 2026 · Perplexity (assistant) · Proposed implementation brief; not permission to merge/deploy or approve shared knowledge.

## Mission

Build the Commons experience incrementally around existing real capabilities. Visual north star: Cisco Cloud Control look and feel as requested by the user. Interaction principle: a useful investigation that teaches through its actual material, inspired especially by Transformer Explainer. Do not turn this into an architecture dashboard, chat wrapper or mandatory node graph.

## First task: Phase 0, then pause for review

Inspect current apps/commons UI, routes, contracts, service, corpus, tests, deployment configuration and current review. Identify reusable capabilities and changed assumptions. Run the existing relevant checks if possible; record failures and unavailable tooling honestly. Do not rerun historical completed build prompts as current tasks.

Trace 'My Mac cannot see my frame' through a real search result and exact source passage. Produce a scoped baseline and one implemented visual checkpoint on that real journey using the blueprint's Cisco-inspired hierarchy. Preserve application behaviour; do not begin with months of infrastructure or a polished fake workflow.

If visual reference remains ambiguous, request the specific Cisco screenshot/theme while treating proposed tokens as provisional. Do not invent access to an authenticated Cisco product or private styles.

Evaluate TanStack only against the actual starter and current route/auth/service constraints. Recommend incremental integration or retention with reasons. Do not silently migrate framework, add SSR, replace services or reorganise the repository.

Stop after the baseline and first visual checkpoint for human review before extending the design. If repository review status does not permit implementation, provide the scoped proposal first.

## Preserve

Original source wording distinct from interpretation; unknowns; source/author/date/passage links; actual relationship origins; assistance declarations; validation/moderation; corrections/history; browser/repository/CLI/MCP entrances; private-to-shared boundaries; current usable service and corpus. Existing map/timeline/curation can remain available without dominating newcomer entry. Do not delete capabilities merely to simplify the shell.

## First runnable vertical slice after review

Situation -> real search -> relevant account -> evidence/difference -> original source -> back. Add comparison, contribution preview/rediscovery and mechanism inspection in the build plan's later slices, reusing what already exists.

Explain only what the system can substantiate. Do not fabricate match reasons, source passages, lineage stages, compatibility, successful publication, community activity or test passes. Save local draft, submit to shared room and publish externally must remain different actions/statuses.

## Verification and return format

Use current package scripts, not assumed commands. Verify route/back/reload, old entrances, keyboard/focus, narrow/wide layout, reduced motion, contrast, stale responses and loading/empty/error/partial/unsupported/permission states as relevant.

Return:
- Scope and capability delivered.
- Existing work reused and contract changes, with rationale.
- Changed files and reviewable commit/PR.
- Commands run and actual results; screenshots where available.
- Unverified checks and known limitations.
- Open decisions and the next bounded slice.

No automatic merge, deployment, external posting, source-repository modifications or human review records. Follow repository proposal/write-back rules and runtime confirmation requirements. Future phases are proposals, not blanket authorisation to execute everything.
